chunks: And by this chain of narrators, from Muhammad ibn Uthman, he said: Narrated to us Ahmad, who said: Narrated to us Affan and Yahya ibn Ishaq al-Sailhani, who said: Narrated to us Hammad ibn Salama, who said: Narrated to us Abdullah ibn Uthman from Abi Tufayl, who said: Abdullah ibn Umar said to me:
Then there will be the Naqf and the Naqaf.

key_terms.أَبُو الطُّفَيْلِ: Abi Tufayl, a companion of the Prophet
key_terms.النَّقْفُ وَالنَّقَافُ: Naqf and Naqaf, terms indicating mischief, bloodshed, and strife
key_terms.بَنِي كَعْبِ بْنِ لُؤَيٍّ: Descendants of Ka'b ibn Lu'ay, referring to the Quraysh tribe
key_terms.عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ عُمَرَ: Abdullah ibn Umar, a prominent companion of the Prophet

ai.seo_question: Who are the twelve caliphs from Banu Ka'b ibn Lu'ay mentioned by Abdullah ibn Umar?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* highlights the Sunni consensus on the twelve Caliphs, serving as a foundational proof for the number of Imams in Shia theology. The mention of 'Naqf and Naqaf' following the twelve leaders is interpreted by scholars as a period of civil strife and deviation, underscoring the transition from guided leadership to temporal power struggles.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: H 95 - It is narrated from the same chains of narrators from Muhammad bin Uthman that: Narrated to us Ahmad that: Narrated to us Affan and Yahya bin Ishaq Sailhini that: Narrated to us Hammad bin Salma that: Narrated to us Abdullah bin Uthman from Abi Tufayl that: Abdullah bin Umar said to me: O Aba Tufayl,

you must consider twelve persons from the descendants of Kaab bin Loi as the Caliphs of the Messenger of Allah (s), after whom mischief and bloodshed would occur and people would fight each other [as all those who mention the twelve persons would create a great controversy].
